decisions.statement: The tests a change is judged by are the ones standing beside the files the change has.
A test beside no changed file is left red rather than made input.
A test another file's change breaks is a test in the wrong file.
A module loaded from two trees at once is two modules.
The run reads a body the change has whether or not a file is at that path.
The run reads the change's bodies through an overlay mounted over the checkout.
A body the change answers nothing for is a path the overlay takes away.
A test file taken away after the check read it is run on the body that read got.
The run reads the index this change leaves rather than the index HEAD holds.
That index reaches the run as bodies over the checkout.
The change's own bodies reach the run that way too.
An entry file the change empties is a path the overlay takes away too.
A manifest the change has is reached under the name that manifest states.
That name is a link the overlay makes onto the folder the manifest sits in.
A manifest calling its package nothing is reached under no name.
The manifest at the repository root is reached under no name.
A page type the change moves is resolved by the run at the path the change files that type at.
A test stands beside a changed file when the change answers a body for the test.
The verdict is read from the lines the run printed rather than from its exit code alone.
A run reaching fewer files than that run named has failed.
A change with no file with a test beside that file is judged by no run.
A file the index files a test beside is input to the check.
A change with only a test runs that test.
No test is named for a file whose test does not stand beside that file.
A test may reach the gate.
The marker saying a run is going descends every process that run starts.
A run already inside a run refuses rather than saying the tests passed.
That refusal says no test ran and what says a run is already going.
A run already inside a run refuses nothing where the change names no test.
Whatever was written to mount the bodies is swept whatever the run said.
A change with a test file costing above the ceiling that file has is refused.
That refusal names each file over the ceiling.
That refusal names the seconds each file over the ceiling spent.
A refusal names the ceiling those seconds are read against.
A run ended at its ceiling with no file over on its own says so rather than blaming the runner.
That refusal says the tests themselves are green.
A slow run is reported against the first file over the ceiling.
A run told to measure has every test file named to no ceiling.
A measuring run answers each file beside the seconds that file spent.
A measuring run refuses whatever the tests said.
Nothing lands.
A file whose measured run came back unclean is said to be unclean.
No measuring run says whether the tests passed.
The whole output of the run is in the refusal.
The color the runner painted the output with is taken out.
A blank line the runner printed is taken out.
No count of lines is kept from the output.
How much of a refusal one answer has is settled where the apply answers.
A run that failed is reported against the first file its output blames.
A short run and a crashed run are reported that way too.
The output blames a file only where the runner reported a failure under that file's name.
The runner reports a failure by a failed test line or an unhandled error line.
An error a test logs is printed just as the runner prints an error.
A header for a file the run did not name takes the blame off the file named before it.
A run whose output blames no file is reported against the first file named.
A refusal blaming no file says the file it names is not the file that failed.
A refusal says how many errors the run raised outside any test.
A refusal names a file that errored as errored rather than as failed.
That refusal says deleting a test nothing needs is the best way to make a file cheaper.
What one test file's run cost is recorded beside the page that test file is of.
Every file of one run is recorded under the one run id.
Each file is recorded as the run of that file says its peak was measured.
A file that came back unclean is recorded with one refusal.
A measuring run records what each file cost as a judging run does.
A cost is recorded whether the run passed or was refused.
A cost that could not be recorded leaves the check's answer as that answer was.
A test file the change brings whose page has not landed is recorded nowhere.
No total holds a run.
Each test file is held to the ceiling its property states.
A total would fall only by having fewer tests rather than by any test being faster.
A fixture shaped like the runner's output says in its name whether that shape was captured.
A captured fixture keeps the shape a run printed, with the paths restated.
A path restated that way names no file this repository has.
A folder move respells a real path, and leaves a fixture naming one stale.
The bodies the overlay carries are the ones the change names as carried, or the changed ones.
A test file the run named that the tree the run read has nowhere is refused by naming that file.
That refusal says whether the overlay carried a removal for the file or carried no body for it.
That refusal says the name is right and renaming the file mends nothing.
That refusal is filed against the first file the tree had nowhere.

definition: the check refusing a change whose tests do not pass
